_notes: THE STARTUP CHARGE, A FIFTH LAYER ADDED AFTER THE PILOT SHIPPED. Read
Assets/_Project/Art/Sheets/Spells/prismatic_bolt/CHARGE_HANDOFF.md for the
brief this follows: a caster-side gather-then-release beat that plays
before the flight core opens.
SIX CELLS, IN ORDER, NOTHING COMPOSED -- the same shape as *_core.json.
water_charge_6f.png is 1536x1024 over 3 columns by 2 rows and divides
exactly into 512px cells, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom per the
handoff. No rects, no canvas, no scale steps: frames 1-5 gather and
compress, frame 6 is the rightward release accent, all six preserved on
disk even though skills.json's authored `seconds` on the charge layer
stops the played CLIP one frame short of frame 6's full hold (see that
file for why -- the crossfade needs frame 6 to start FADING the instant
it appears, not to play out first).
DELIVERED WITH ITS OWN ALPHA (built-in image generation, RGBA preserved
per the handoff), so keyed is false like the rest of the pack.
MEASURED, NOT REUSED: the core's own painted bounds (water_core_6f.png)
fill about 74% of their 512 canvas at every frame; this sheet's condensed
seed (frames 3-5) fills only 22-30%, with the gathering/release frames
reaching 41% at their widest. skills.json sizes the charge layer well
under the core's own box for exactly that reason -- see its own comment
for the arithmetic.
ALPHA EDGES: soft throughout, as the handoff warns for every element --
measured, none of the six cells reach full 255 opacity even at the
densest bead (max ~254, mostly soft gradient). Read as intended painterly
glow rather than a keying defect; Wind is the sheet where this actually
reads as washed-out (see that recipe's notes).
